articles.title: Device Database plans community edits and richer device pages
articles.dek: An expanded contribution plan keeps reported facts separate from community additions; a launch proposal targets early 2027.
body: The Open Home Foundation plans to let people correct model information and add images to existing Device Database entries. Its expanded roadmap brings community contributions and richer pages into one effort, while exploring a public launch beyond Preview in early 2027.

Matthias Kerstner rewrites the contribution opportunity to include the richer-pages work that previously had its own proposal. Website edits and direct contributions to the public repository would share review and attribution, with a GitHub account required initially. The first editable fields cover images, model, model ID, category and brand; overviews, references and galleries are also in scope.

Facts reported by Home Assistant would remain visibly separate from community additions. Information from other public databases would enter as suggestions for contributors to accept. The plan calls for one importer to demonstrate the process; moderation rules, conflicting information and image rights still need resolution.

Kerstner’s separate launch proposal remains in Considering and targets leaving Preview and OHF Labs in the first quarter of 2027. Contributions, visual design and branding, and legal review must come together first. The quarter is a planning target; using the data inside Home Assistant and through a public API sits outside this launch scope.

externalSources.title: Stage 3: Enable contributions to enrich device pages
Establish richer device pages to provide more contextual information
Launch public version of the Device Database

articles.title: Apple Watch reports its own location to Home Assistant
articles.dek: Each connected home can receive an exact location, a zone alone or no location at all.
body: Home Assistant’s Apple Watch app reports the watch’s own location instead of leaving its device tracker unknown. A setting for each connected server offers Exact, Zone only or Never, with sharing off by default.
Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves adds updates when the watch app opens and during background refresh. The setting controls what each home receives; it does not promise continuous tracking.

pullRequests.title: Add location reporting to Apple Watch device tracker

articles.title: ESPHome stops moving Hörmann doors before another command
articles.dek: Rapid commands stop a moving garage door instead of reversing it or restarting it after a stop.
body: ESPHome changes how it controls Hörmann garage doors: a command to change direction, position or ventilation while the door moves only stops it. Commands in quick succession therefore cannot reverse the door at speed, and a repeated stop no longer starts it again.

Raphael Hehl sends each command once and checks the reported movement before sending a stop. Lamp requests use an explicit on or off state rather than counting toggles; a request made during movement waits until the door stops. Hehl tested opening, closing, repeated stops, ventilation and lamp control on a Series 4 motor.

pullRequests.title: [hoermann_hcp] Send each command once, and the lamp as a state
[hoermann_hcp] Commands only stop a moving door

articles.title: Home Assistant starts Music Assistant podcasts at the newest episode
articles.dek: An ordinary playback action replaces an administrator-token workaround and can also start playlists at a chosen track.
body: Home Assistant automations gain a way to start a Music Assistant podcast at its newest episode instead of queuing from the oldest one. The playback action accepts latest or newest as a starting item, bringing a Music Assistant capability into the normal Home Assistant action.

Trevor Baker tested the change with Music Assistant 2.10.5 and a Sonos Arc: a news podcast started with the latest bulletin rather than its old trailer. It also accepts a track or episode identifier, or part of its name, to start an album or playlist at that item.

This is Baker’s first contribution to Home Assistant Core, reviewed by Marcel van der Veldt. It removes the need for the separately configured request with an administrator token previously suggested for this task.

pullRequests.title: Add start_item to Music Assistant's play_media action

articles.title: Home Assistant starts even when Supervisor’s own update fails
articles.dek: A failed automatic update stops leaving Core and installed apps permanently unstarted.
body: Home Assistant continues starting when Supervisor’s automatic startup update fails. Previously, a failed image download could leave Supervisor indefinitely in its startup state, with Home Assistant Core and apps never started.

Manuel Rüger makes startup wait for the update’s result and continue when it fails or cannot begin. A successful Supervisor update keeps its existing handover behavior. Stefan Agner reviewed the correction.

pullRequests.title: Await Supervisor auto update task during startup

articles.title: Sendspin’s command-line player streams microphone and line-in audio
articles.dek: Linux and macOS capture bring the earlier C++ library work into a configurable desktop tool.
body: Sendspin’s command-line player gains an audio input option for sending a microphone or line-in to a compatible server. Linux supports ALSA, PipeWire and PulseAudio inputs, while macOS uses CoreAudio. The input is optional and can run alongside the player’s existing audio output.

Chris builds on the C++ audio-input support reported on October 6. A Mac test sent audible microphone audio to Music Assistant, including the macOS permission prompt. Linux tests verified capture and device recovery; streaming that capture to a server remains untested.

A named Linux input stays tied to that device instead of silently switching to the default if it disappears. Mac users should make their first run from Terminal.app so the microphone permission prompt can appear.

Add CoreAudio capture: --input coreaudio on macOS
Capture through PipeWire and PulseAudio with --input

articles.title: ESPHome lets makers design a device’s guided setup
articles.dek: Firmware can describe setup pages and household entity choices for Home Assistant 2026.11.
body: ESPHome lets device makers describe a guided setup for Home Assistant, highlighting the settings that matter and asking the owner to choose the household entities the device needs. A device can define several pages instead of leaving someone to work through a long list of controls.

Jesse Hills supplies the firmware and client support. A maker can expose selected device settings, connect a sensor or control to an entity chosen in Home Assistant, or ask for an entity used by a custom action. The configuration decides which entity types are valid choices.
The guide specifies Home Assistant 2026.11 for showing these pages. This adds choices defined by the device maker, beyond the general capability checklist reported on October 1.

Add device wizard support

[api] Note that the setup wizard needs Home Assistant 2026.11

articles.title: Music Assistant plays personal collections from Yandex Disk
articles.dek: A new connection browses and streams music, audiobooks and podcasts with read-only access.
body: Music Assistant adds Yandex Disk as a source for personal music, audiobooks and podcasts. The connection browses and synchronizes the cloud-stored collection and streams its files through Music Assistant.
Mikhail Nevskiy uses Yandex’s device sign-in flow with the listener’s own application registration and read-only Disk access. OzGav reviewed the addition.

pullRequests.title: Add Yandex Disk provider

articles.title: ESPHome warns that Intel Mac support ends by June 2027
articles.dek: The 2027.6.0 release is the latest planned cutoff, and dependency changes could bring it forward.
body: ESPHome warns people building firmware on Intel Macs that support will end with version 2027.6.0 or earlier. The notice appears on every run and in the Intel option on the installation page, giving those users a deadline for moving their build environment.

J. Nick Koston explains that required Python packages are dropping Intel macOS builds. ESPHome already holds some dependencies at older versions for those computers, but a security correction or incompatible change could make that approach impossible before June.

pullRequests.title: [core] Warn on every run that Intel Mac support ends by 2027.6.0
Note that Intel Mac support ends by 2027.6.0

articles.title: Music Assistant protects private playlists from other members’ AI clients
articles.dek: The playlist resource now checks who is allowed to read it.
body: Music Assistant closes a privacy gap in its connection for AI clients: a household member could request another member’s private playlist by its identifier. The playlist resource loaded the saved access record without enforcing it.

Mikhail Nevskiy makes the resource enforce the caller’s permission, treating a hidden playlist like a missing one. Marvin Schenkel reviewed the correction. It addresses a specific disclosure alongside the command-access controls reported on October 6.

pullRequests.title: Update FastMCP Server provider to v2.1.24

articles.title: ESPHome guides signed devices through their first custom installation
articles.dek: Device Builder explains when a USB cable is needed instead of offering a wireless update the device will reject.
body: ESPHome Device Builder directs the first custom installation on a device with vendor-signed firmware to USB. After adopting such a device, the owner’s build is normally unsigned, so attempting to install it wirelessly is rejected by the firmware’s signature check.

Keith Burzinski makes the installation dialog explain the requirement and disables the wireless route. Adoption keeps the existing hostname until that first USB installation, avoiding a rename that would also attempt a wireless update. After unsigned firmware is installed, wireless installation is offered again.
Burzinski tested the flow on a Home Assistant Connect AUX-2. This is his first contribution to the Device Builder frontend, reviewed by J. Nick Koston.

articles.title: Home Assistant blocks apps from bypassing system permissions with batched commands
articles.dek: Supervisor checks every command before forwarding a batch with Home Assistant’s privileged access.
body: Home Assistant’s Supervisor closes a route for installed apps to make privileged system changes, such as adding an app repository. An app allowed to use the Home Assistant connection could wrap a prohibited command inside a batch and have it forwarded with Core’s more privileged identity.

Mike Degatano makes Supervisor inspect each command and reject the whole batch if any command is prohibited or cannot be verified. Batches containing only allowed commands continue to work. Stefan Agner reviewed the correction.

pullRequests.title: Reject WebSocket batches containing denied commands in the HA proxy

articles.title: Home Assistant preserves custom settings when configuring managed apps
articles.dek: Starting a stopped Z-Wave JS app no longer resets options such as its radio region and logging choices.
body: Home Assistant preserves settings that an integration does not manage when it configures an app. Previously, preparing a stopped Z-Wave JS app could replace the whole configuration, discarding the owner’s radio-region and logging choices, including during setup after an update.
Contributor AlCalzone keeps the existing options and changes only those supplied by the integration. Martin Hjelmare reviewed the correction.

pullRequests.title: Fix managed app configuration resetting existing options

articles.title: Four Zooz and Aqara devices join Home Assistant’s certified list
articles.dek: The additions cover a dimmer, high-power relay, power strip and Matter-over-Thread lock.
body: The Works with Home Assistant catalog adds four certified devices: Zooz’s ZEN56 RGBW Dimmer, ZEN78 Long Range High Power Relay and ZEN20 Power Strip, plus Aqara’s U400 smart lock using Matter over Thread.

The listings place all three Zooz devices in the United States, Canada and Mexico, and the Aqara lock in the United States and Canada. Miranda Bishop makes her first contribution to the certification website with the additions, reviewed by dan-long-dev. These are certification listings, rather than new integration implementations.

pullRequests.title: Add newly certified Zooz and Aqara devices

articles.title: Sonos group control survives the television waking up
articles.dek: Music Assistant keeps control when the television changes which speaker leads a Sonos group.
body: A correction in Music Assistant’s Sonos library prevents a television waking up from leaving a speaker group playing but uncontrollable. Sonos can move control of an existing group to another speaker without changing the group’s identity; the library had failed to start following the new controlling speaker.

Michael N reproduced the failure with a Sonos Arc and a three-speaker group using Music Assistant 2.10.5 with the modified library. The corrected library followed the new controlling speaker in the test. This is Michael N’s first contribution to aiosonos, reviewed by Marcel van der Veldt.

roadmapUpdates.title: Automation target exclusions receive approval
roadmapUpdates.summary: Franck Nijhof approves Niels’s proposal to exclude individual entities from area, floor or label targets and assigns it Low priority. The planned exclusions persist as group membership changes; approval does not set a release date.

sources.title: Let users exclude individual entities from resolved targets in automations/blueprints/scripts

roadmapUpdates.title: Modbus connection overview is marked complete
roadmapUpdates.summary: Matthias Kerstner marks the Modbus panel opportunity Done, crediting Paulus Schoutsen’s work. The plan brings connection health and connected devices into Connectivity settings; this roadmap update does not establish a release.

sources.title: Show a Modbus panel in the new Connectivity settings to provide an easy entry point

roadmapUpdates.title: ESPHome setup wizard is flagged as an AUX2 dependency
roadmapUpdates.summary: The roadmap now labels the ESPHome setup wizard an “AUX2 blocker.” The work remains in Building and already carried an At Risk delivery status; its checklist is intended to guide setup of the capabilities a device exposes.

sources.title: Introduce an "ESPHome device setup wizard" to ease setup and configuration of ESPHome devices through their capabilities - AUX2 blocker
